reading.title: Folding a Paper Crane
reading.purpose: Learn about the art of origami and why a handmade paper crane can mean so much.
paras: Paper folding is called origami. It is a famous art in Japan, and one of its best-known shapes is the paper crane. A real crane is a tall bird that lives near quiet water, so many people think of it as a peaceful bird.
Its long neck and wide wings make a graceful shape. Folders try to copy those smooth, beautiful lines. A crane is flawless when every fold is sharp and the paper has no tears.

Beginners may think the job is hopeless, because the paper bends the wrong way. Then they gradually get better, a little more with each try. After many tries, an expert's hands can move swiftly through all of the steps.
Folding can also help a restless child learn to sit still and focus. A fearless folder does not give up after a mistake. She just takes a new sheet and starts again.

A paper crane makes a thoughtful gift, because it shows that you care about someone's feelings. To the person who gets it, a handmade crane can be priceless, worth more than anything that money can buy.

qs.q: In paragraph 3, a beginner who thinks the job is "hopeless" feels that it
choices: is much too easy to be fun
has no chance of working out
will take only a minute or two
needs far more paper than anyone has
qs.why: The beginner thinks the job is hopeless because the paper bends the wrong way, so it seems it will never work.

qs.q: Which sentence tells why a paper crane makes a thoughtful gift?
choices: A crane is flawless when every fold is sharp and the paper has no tears.
Folding can also help a restless child learn to sit still and focus.
A paper crane makes a thoughtful gift, because it shows that you care about someone's feelings.
qs.why: This sentence gives the reason: the gift shows that you care about how someone feels.

ev.text: A paper crane makes a thoughtful gift, because it shows that you care about someone's feelings.

qs.q: Why does a fearless folder take a new sheet and start again?
choices: A crane must always be folded from a new sheet that has never been used.
She is angry at the first sheet and tears it into many little pieces.
Mistakes do not scare her, so she keeps trying until it works.
An expert told her that a new sheet is always faster than fixing a fold.
qs.why: The reading says a fearless folder does not give up after a mistake, so she tries again.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Folding a crane takes practice, and the finished crane can mean a lot to someone.
Paper cranes are the only shape that people in Japan have ever folded from paper.
Real cranes are easy to fold from paper because they live near quiet water and are tall.
Beginners should not try origami because the paper always bends the wrong way.
qs.why: The reading describes how a crane is folded, how folders improve, and why a crane makes a special gift.
